test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Identify the INCORRECT statement in the context of Microfinance Institutions in India.

options.text: A microfinance loan is given to a household having annual household income up to Rs. 3,00,000.
A microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan.
When giving a micro loan, a household means an individual family unit, i.e., husband, wife, and their unmarried children.
A microfinance loan should be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A microfinance loan should be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **A microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan, meaning that it does not require any lien on the borrower's deposit account.**
 
• Microfinance institutions provide small loans to low-income households and individuals who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• The annual household income limit for microfinance loans in India is up to **Rs. 3,00,000.**
 
• Microfinance loans are collateral-free, meaning that they do not require any security or guarantor for the loan.
 
• **Microfinance loans are given to households, which typically include the husband, wife, and their unmarried children.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Microfinance institutions in India play a crucial role in providing financial services to the unbanked population and promoting financial inclusion.
 
• Microfinance loans are usually given for income-generating activities such as **small businesses, agriculture, and livestock rearing.**
 
• Microfinance institutions also provide other financial services such as **savings accounts, insurance, and remittances.**
 
• **In recent years, microfinance institutions in India have faced challenges such as over-indebtedness, high interest rates, and aggressive loan recovery practices, leading to concerns about the welfare of borrowers.**
